brief.headline: We pay ₹66.48/KG — 55% above the India export benchmark of ₹42.95/KG; with ₹15.03 Cr spend (1.38% of their revenue), negotiate down toward market line or secure volume rebate

priceAsk.summary: Target a 20–30% reduction to close the gap between our ₹66.48/KG and the India export unit value of ₹42.95/KG
priceAsk.target: Move from ₹66.48/KG toward the market line of ₹42.95/KG
priceAsk.basis: We are currently paying ₹66.48/KG against a public India export benchmark of ₹42.95/KG — a significant premium. Our ₹15.03 Cr annual volume (1.38% of their ₹1087.88 Cr revenue) justifies direct-manufacturer pricing closer to export parity

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to move from 30 Days After Receipt to advance or COD in exchange for a corresponding price discount
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Shifting to advance payment frees ₹1.24 Cr of our working capital currently tied up; a 15-day acceleration alone is worth ₹61.76 L

brief.financialLeverage: Sayaji's net margin is razor-thin at 1.1% and EBITDA margin 4.9%, well below what healthy suppliers run. Debt-to-equity stands at 2.37x, so they are carrying significant leverage. Our ₹15.03 Cr represents 1.38% of their ₹1087.88 Cr revenue — a meaningful customer that they cannot easily replace. Their D (18/100) health score signals fragility: push firmly on price to close the market-line gap, but frame any hard ask around volume commitment and faster cash to avoid tipping a stretched supplier into distress.

evidence.point: We pay a large premium over the India export benchmark for Dextrose
We are a top-tier customer by revenue share
evidence.figure: Our ₹15.03 Cr is 1.38% of their ₹1087.88 Cr revenue

evidence.point: Sayaji operates on extremely thin margins
They carry heavy debt relative to equity
Faster payment terms free meaningful working capital for us
evidence.figure: 30-day terms tie up ₹1.24 Cr; 15-day acceleration frees ₹61.76 L

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker with health score B (62/100) and revenue ₹2359.06 Cr — established dextrose supplier and a financially stronger drop-in alternate

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (starch, dextrose) with revenue ₹821.13 Cr and health score C (53/100) — growing capacity and a credible second source

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore maize wet-miller producing Dextrose ANHYDROUS (IV-fluid grade) with revenue ₹365.39 Cr — exact form match, though health score D (27/100) requires CoA verification

risks: Sayaji's 1.1% net margin and D (18/100) health score mean an aggressive price squeeze could destabilize supply — balance the ask with volume or payment-term sweeteners
High debt-to-equity of 2.37x is a continuity watch — if they stumble financially mid-year, we risk disruption on a sole-source material
We already pay Sayaji our best price at ₹66.48/KG (0.0% gap vs. best), so any concession will require a fresh negotiation rather than parity with another vendor
Three credible alternates exist, but onboarding pharma-grade dextrose (CoA, IP monograph compliance) takes 3–6 months — use the threat, but keep Sayaji stable in the interim
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership and want to lock in volume, but at ₹66.48/KG we're paying 55% over the India export line of ₹42.95/KG — let's work together to close that gap and discuss faster payment in exchange for a better rate.
